entries.title: 30 more player skins — Dream SMP, MCC & YouTubers
entries.summary: PlayerMobs can now spawn wearing 30 additional real-player skins from the Minecraft streaming and MCC scene — Dream, Technoblade, CaptainSparklez, LDShadowLady, Skeppy and more — bringing the custom-skin pool to 68. Recognizable real-player skins also show up more often: a naturally-spawned PlayerMob now has a 40% chance (up from 30%) of wearing one instead of a vanilla default.
highlights: 30 new skins (pool now 68): Dream SMP, MCC players, and Minecraft YouTubers
Recognizable real-player skins now appear ~40% of the time, up from ~30%
Each skin renders with its correct slim or wide arm model

entries.title: Loved PlayerMobs travel with you on the Dungeon Train
entries.summary: On a Dungeon Train, a PlayerMob that has come to love you now abandons its own fixed route and makes its way to your carriage, settling in once it's with you. Move on down the train and it follows; step off the train and it stays aboard and goes back to its usual wandering.
highlights: A PlayerMob that loves you heads to your carriage instead of marching its own way
Uses the full train toolkit to reach you — stepping through rooms, leaping carriage-group gaps, opening doors, and digging through fill
Relaxes and does its own thing once it shares your carriage; resumes its route if you leave the train
Toggle with the new trainFollowLovedPlayer config option (on by default)

entries.title: Reincarnated echoes wear the player's real skin
entries.summary: "Echo of <name>" PlayerMobs on the Dungeon Train now show the real skin of the player they're an echo of, instead of a default Steve/Alex skin. Their name was already right — now their look matches too.
highlights: Dungeon-Train echoes match the skin of the player they came from
Also fixes the friend-echoes that travel alongside them
The skin is captured at the moment of death, so each echo looks like that player did then

entries.title: Reincarnations can come from other mods
entries.summary: PlayerMob now has a two-way reincarnation bridge other mods can plug into: a companion mod can both add past lives — including players from other worlds — to the pool a PlayerMob may return as, and read PlayerMob's death log. Local and remote reincarnations roll on separate chances, so meeting players from elsewhere never reduces your chance of meeting your own past lives. With no such mod installed nothing changes — except that Dungeon Train echoes now lean toward your more recent past lives.
highlights: Other mods can contribute past lives to the reincarnation pool — a spawning PlayerMob can come back as a life from an integrating mod, not just PlayerMob's own death log.
Players from other worlds can turn up as echoes in yours (and you in theirs) — a remote echo is always someone else, never you.
Local and remote echoes roll separately, so a remote pool never eats into your own past-life reincarnations.
Other mods can read PlayerMob's death log (who died, where, and their skin, gear and traits).
Dungeon Train echoes now favour your more recent deaths, with a mild lean toward lives that ended near your current depth.

entries.title: Integration seam to steer a PlayerMob's train march
entries.summary: Adds a small compatibility seam (TrainConfinement.setMarchDirection) that lets a Dungeon-Train host set a freshly-spawned PlayerMob's fixed march direction along the train, overriding its normal boarding choice. PlayerMob's own behaviour is unchanged; Dungeon Train uses this so a PlayerMob can be spawned already heading your way.
highlights: New compat API: TrainConfinement.setMarchDirection(mob, dir) plus PlayerMobEntity.setTrainExploreDir(int).

entries.title: Echo-spawn modding seam
entries.summary: Adds a modding hook so an integrating mod can react the moment a PlayerMob spawns as a reincarnated echo — Dungeon Train uses it to chronicle cross-world echo encounters.
highlights: New PlayerMobSpawnHooks seam reports each echo spawn with its source life and whether it came from a local or remote (cross-world) pool.

entries.title: Personality now colours how PlayerMobs feel about you
entries.summary: A PlayerMob's friendliness and aggression now shape how strongly it reacts to you, not just how it behaves. The friendlier a mob, the more it warms to acts of kindness — gifts, bows, and being defended land harder. The more aggressive a mob, the less it cares about being struck — a hot-tempered fighter shrugs off a blow that would turn a gentler mob against you.
highlights: Friendly mobs warm up to twice as fast from gifts, bows, and rescues (×1.0 at minimum friendliness rising to ×2.0 at maximum).
Aggressive mobs barely hold a grudge for being hit, while timid mobs take it to heart (×0.2 at maximum aggression up to ×1.2 at minimum).
The Aggressive archetype is now both hard to befriend and slow to anger when struck; the Friendly archetype bonds quickly but is more easily hurt.

entries.title: PlayerMob now runs on Minecraft 1.20.1
entries.summary: PlayerMob now ships a build for Minecraft 1.20.1 (Fabric and Forge), alongside the existing 1.21.1 build. It's the same player-shaped, weapon-aware mob — now playable on 1.20.1 worlds.
highlights: New 1.20.1 build for Fabric and Forge.
NeoForge 1.20.1 users: the Forge jar works on NeoForge 1.20.1.
1.21.1 builds (Fabric, Forge, NeoForge) are unchanged — grab the jar matching your Minecraft version + loader.

entries.title: PlayerMob now runs on the latest Minecraft (26.2)
entries.summary: PlayerMob now ships a build for Minecraft 26.2 'Chaos Cubed' (Fabric and NeoForge), on top of the existing 1.20.1 and 1.21.1 builds. It's the same player-shaped, weapon-aware mob — now on the latest Minecraft.
highlights: New 26.2 build for Fabric and NeoForge.
PlayerMob now covers Minecraft 1.20.1, 1.21.1, and 26.2 — grab the jar matching your version + loader.
NeoForge 26.2 is still in beta upstream, so treat the 26.2 build as a preview.
